Sixteen Cycles ago, in Cycle 99, the Oakland Oaks front office selected center Wendell Carter Jr. in the expansion draft to anchor a switchable, defensive core, while trading assets to secure the number one overall pick to draft scoring forward AJ Dybantsa and targeting undrafted point guard Adash Stanley (*C83-c107 Master Timeline*; *c99_supplemental_Oaks_expansion_draft.md*). Roster architecture reports confirmed the franchise planned an aggressive identity featuring physical perimeter disruptors, including Dillon Brooks, alongside Stanley's high-motor playmaking (*C83-c107 Master Timeline*; *Oakland Oaks*). Fourteen Cycles ago, in Cycle 101, reporting established that the team's on-court core would orbit around Stanley and Dybantsa as head coach Wilson Shepard installed his motion offense (*bay_tribune_e101.pdf*).

Seven Cycles ago, in Cycle 108, the Oaks dropped their preseason opener, with Dybantsa posting 18 points and 11 rebounds as Shepard acknowledged the expansion roster was still working through its rotational kinks and chemistry (*The Cycle Pulse — Y2C108*). Five Cycles ago, in Cycle 110, the Oaks concluded an 0–5 preseason, dropping consecutive games despite Dybantsa producing scoring lines of 22 and 11 points and Stanley contributing an 11-assist finale (*The Cycle Pulse — Y2C110*). Sports beat analysts questioned how individual scoring would connect across games, leaving unresolved whether early statistical flashes were foundational or merely situational (*The Cycle Pulse — Y2C110*).

One Cycle ago, in Cycle 114, the Oaks rallied from a 20-point deficit on the road before falling 104–100 in Indiana, then answered by routing Toronto 135–75 and beating Oklahoma City 101–95 at home to improve to 6–1 (*The Cycle Pulse — Y3C10*). Prior published coverage contained no reporting on second-round rookie Harry Hayward or T. Jerome before Cycle 115.
